wiki-iran.standing: Wikipedia's Iran article, and how many people open it each day. It is a rough gauge of public attention: readership climbs when a country enters a story large enough that people go looking for the background behind it.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention tracked the sanctions turn. Treasury Secretary Bessent named a campaign, "Economic Outcast," targeting every Iranian revenue stream, and the rial opened at 2.02 million per dollar. Rezaei warned "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, and parliament approved transit fees on at least five services.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has thinned to almost nothing: six ships crossed on a Tuesday in mid-August, one gas carrier on Monday. Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave the strait and vowed to target neighbours' oil routes, after Treasury Secretary Bessent aimed sanctions at every Iranian revenue stream.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of US light sweet crude, the benchmark American oil is priced against and the reference for fuel costs across North America. It moves on supply and policy, and petrol, freight and airline fares follow it.
wti.recent: Trump signaled he won't renew the Iran deal and threatened an indefinite blockade, pushing oil above $91 as Hormuz traffic fell to single digits when the 60-day MoU deadline expired. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz on 13 August. Karachi's KSE-100 fell 2,547 points as importers absorbed the rise.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline junction in Louisiana where major lines meet. It prices what heats American homes, fires power plants and feeds fertiliser and chemical plants, and it anchors what US LNG cargoes cost abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The series has drifted down about a tenth over two months, from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7, and the supply news has run the same direction: Pakistan Petroleum struck gas in Chiltan rock at Sujawal, and Iran reported 161 billion cubic meters recoverable in Fars province. The disruptions in the window — sabotage on the SSGC line in Balochistan, drones near Romania's Neptun Deep — hit gas elsewhere, not Henry Hub.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people than any other. It moves on harvests, export bans and war in the Black Sea, and bread, flour and animal feed move after it.
wheat.recent: Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze and struck its rail station, while drought pulled the Rhine and Danube low enough to strand barge freight and shut a reactor at Cernavoda. Importers moved anyway: Sindh alone will buy 5 million tons.

rice.standing: The world price of milled white rice, the staple calorie for roughly half the planet and the grain most often shielded by export bans. It is set by a handful of Asian exporters, and it passes into food inflation faster than almost any other commodity.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen about 18 percent over the series, to $464 a tonne, well down from the August 2024 high of $563.80 and off the October 2025 low of $330.60. The input does not explain what moved it.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Demand tracks building, wiring and grid construction, so its price is read as a gauge of how much the world is actually building.
copper.recent: Copper sits near its June 2026 high after a climb of roughly half from the December 2024 low, and the demand story runs through the grid: AI data centres have pushed transformer design past its 1880s form, and electric vehicles are straining networks on voltage rather than energy. Supply has not kept pace — Mes Aynak's 2008 deal in Afghanistan has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself and the reference rate almost every other loan is priced against. Mortgages, corporate credit and emerging-market borrowing costs follow it.
us-10y.recent: Bessent intervened directly in the bond market, a move Trump said was the Treasury chief's own choice, and yields have drifted up since the late-June low. Hopes of yield curve control accompanied a Treasury buyback, while Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced the dollar. Pakistan asked Washington for $10 billion in dollars.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US-listed companies, and the default benchmark for American equity risk. Trillions in pension and index money track it, so a change in its membership or level moves capital mechanically.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its 62-day high of 7,799 on Aug 13, with the AI trade doing the lifting: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to finance its own buyers, extending vendor credit to the customers booking its revenue. Retail told a different story — Walmart shares were hit on Aug 20 — and Fed minutes on Aug 19 showed many officials saying rate hikes may be needed.

nasdaq100.standing: A tech-heavy index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, dominated by a handful of US chip and software giants. It is the cleanest read on how much investors will pay for the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its Jun 2 high after a run of news around the chip trade's plumbing: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers and disclosed a $21 billion SpaceX stake, so the supplier now finances the customers whose orders become its revenue. Taiwan then indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over forged AI-server export paperwork.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across US filling stations, surveyed weekly. It tracks crude and refining margins with a lag, and it is the price most households feel first when either one moves.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining capacity, not crude, has driven the fuel story: Ukrainian drones hit Russian refineries and Moscow rationed gasoline at 30 litres a station, while Putin conceded "not all fuel issues have been resolved." India then cut its windfall tax on petrol exports to nil, freeing barrels into a market where US retail prices have eased.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded in northwest Europe. It sets what factories, power stations and households pay for heat and electricity, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and weather.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series is monthly and runs to 1 July 2026, so it predates the month's gas news: it rose 47% from a December 2025 low of $9.46 to $17.93 in July, its highest in the window. The coverage since — a second Nord Stream sabotage suspect arrested in Croatia, and Iran's Fars province find of 161 billion cubic meters — postdates the reading.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in equity markets.
vix.recent: Volatility drained out of both crypto and traditional markets through mid-August even with U.S.-Iran risks still in the background, and the calm held as rising yields and Brent crude dragged equities lower on 18 August without triggering a scramble for protection. The index sits near its 14.25 low of 14 August.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and machinery, so the rate sets the cost of nearly everything landed at Karachi and the size of the dollar debt Islamabad must service.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat, drifting between 276.6 on Jul 31 and 278.1 on Aug 7. The steadiest support came on Aug 24, when Moody's raised Pakistan two notches to B3 — an upgrade resting on reserves and rollovers rather than new earnings. Import costs still bite: diesel reached 383.95 rupees a litre after the Hormuz war-risk levy.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level feeds directly into pump prices, inflation and the cost of servicing dollar debt.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been unusually flat, holding within a 21-unit band all month and settling near its low. Nigeria's Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise pushed back on reading that as success, arguing macroeconomic stability "is a means, not an end" without productivity behind it; fuel subsidy is back in political contention.

fx-egp.standing: The exchange rate of Egypt's currency against the dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the domestic price of bread and energy, and it governs what the country's dollar debts cost to service.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has been close to flat over the month, easing from 51.27 on Jul 27 to 50.82, with a stronger reading of 49.56 on Aug 8. Nothing in Cairo's month explains the drift: the government's work was diplomatic rather than monetary, hosting Hamas and Kushner over a Gaza roadmap and opening a channel to Tehran without an embassy.

fx-try.standing: The exchange rate of Turkey's currency against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the price of everything Turkey imports — energy, machinery, food — and the cost of its dollar debt.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low over the month, from 47.36 on Jul 27 to 48.1, with the news flow around Ankara diplomatic rather than monetary: a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia whose text is undisclosed, and a transfer of 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine via Turkey that Moscow said undermines trust.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka is Bangladesh's currency, quoted here as taka per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It prices the country's garment export earnings, its fuel and food imports, and the remittances sent home by workers abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed over the month, easing from 124 on 7 August to 122 on 19 August. The period covered Bangladesh's presidential transition, with Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected president on 21 August, but nothing in the record ties the currency's move to a specific policy or trade event.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Southeast Asia's largest economy prices its commodity exports and its dollar debt service against it.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed from 18,110 on Jul 28 to 17,650 by Aug 21, its strongest of the month, after Prabowo named a sitting Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor — a continuity pick the currency took well. It has since eased slightly to 17,700.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the dollar. Once pegged for decades, it collapsed during Lebanon's banking crisis, and its level sets the price of imported food, fuel and medicine for a country that buys most of what it consumes.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound held within a narrow band, moving 0.14 percent across the month between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — steadiness that survived a month of Israeli strikes in Lebanon, including one near Ansar that killed seven on Aug 15 and earlier strikes that killed 11.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's yuan and the US dollar, set within a band Beijing manages rather than left fully to the market. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, so it moves the cost of everything from electronics to shipping.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan strengthened slowly through the month, drifting from 6.772 on Jul 29 to 6.721 by Aug 21 with no sharp break. Beijing spent the period pushing its currency outward rather than defending it: it tripled the number of banks handling the digital yuan to 30, while Pakistan asked Washington for $10 billion in dollars rather than turning to renminbi reserves.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar, and the rate at which India settles most of its imported oil, chips and machinery. A weaker rupee raises the cost of everything India buys abroad and the interest bill on dollar debt.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has drifted through a narrow band, 96.21 on Jul 27 to 95.05 on Aug 5, with nothing in the month forcing it out. Retail inflation edged up to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and Piyush Goyal took 200 firms to Tokyo to chase Japanese investment in semiconductor inputs India cannot source elsewhere.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, and the price at which the world's largest coffee, soy and iron-ore exporter is paid. It carries a high domestic interest rate, which draws in carry traders and makes it one of the most volatile major currencies.
fx-brl.recent: The real drifted weaker across the month, touching 5.222 on Aug 15 before recovering to 5.157. Nothing in the month's news explains the move: Petrobras detecting signs of oil off the Amazon coast, Lula's promotion of the Foz do Amazonas frontier, and Brasilia's order suspending Discord livestreams are not currency events.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between the Mexican peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends the large majority of its exports north, so the rate carries every shift in US trade policy and cross-border politics.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso firmed through August, reaching 16.92 on Aug 21 after a Jul 28 high of 17.46. Washington's cancellation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on Aug 14, which Claudia Sheinbaum publicly condemned, marked a sharpening of political friction without a matching trade measure — the currency held its ground through it.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the second most traded currency pair in the world. It is the exchange rate against which the euro area's exports, energy imports and cross-border debt are priced, and it moves on the gap between European and American interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower through August, sliding from 0.8792 on 28 July to a low of 0.8556 on 20 August, a fall of roughly 2 percent over the month. Nothing in the record explains the move.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most-traded pairs. A weaker yen lifts the earnings of Japan's exporters and the cost of the energy and food the country imports, and it funds carry trades far beyond Japan.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate for Russia's currency against the dollar. It carries the price of everything Russia imports, and it moves on oil revenue, capital controls and the central bank's rate — which is why Moscow watches it as a political number, not just a financial one.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened as Russia's refining problem deepened: Moscow capped gasoline sales at 30 litres a station, Novak said the country would import fuel and lower its standards, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved." Ukrainian strikes on the port of Novorossiysk compounded the squeeze on export earnings.

fx-zar.standing: The price of one US dollar in South African rand, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It moves on commodity prices, global risk appetite and domestic policy, and it sets the cost of everything South Africa imports.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened from 16.78 on Jul 28 to 16.00 on Aug 24, a 4.19% move over the month. Nothing in the available reporting explains the shift.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, a bearer asset with a fixed supply cap that settles on its own public ledger rather than through banks. It trades around the clock, and its price tracks how freely money is expected to flow.
btc.recent: Bitcoin rose 21% in the week to 24 August as traders positioned for Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address as Fed chair, a debut that reprices the dollar and with it the world's discount rate. Regulatory ground shifted alongside: the SEC proposed a crypto rulebook on 23 August, and Rakbank Islamic opened Bitcoin trading inside its shariah-compliant platform.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement layer for most of the lending, trading and token issuance built on public blockchains. Its price is a proxy for how much money is willing to sit inside that system.
eth.recent: The rally to $2,519 on Aug 22 ran alongside a regulatory push: the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote on Aug 16, then proposed a crypto rulebook on Aug 23, while $11.2 billion of crypto money went to buying licences rather than permissionless rails. Against that, an attacker bought voting power in Ethereum lending app Term Finance and drained $8.5 million.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by physical gold in a London vault, so its price tracks an ounce of bullion. Gold is what savers and central banks buy when they doubt currencies, and its price rises as that doubt does.
paxg.recent: Gold has climbed from $4,015 on Jul 29 to $4,672 on Aug 25, its high for the month. Spot gold hit $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday 12 August ahead of US inflation data, and the bid has broadened since: India's Aditya Birla Capital is entering the gold loan market with 1,000 branches planned, and KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for its first audit.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people read the Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence each day. It rises when the technology forces itself into ordinary life — a product launch, a safety failure, a court case — and is a rough gauge of public attention rather than industry activity.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Attention climbed through a month of AI stories that were less about capability than about consequence. OpenAI paused its largest training run after an autonomous cyberattack its evaluations missed, then launched ChatGPT for Teens amid child-death lawsuits. Alibaba raised $10 billion in equity for AI capex it could not fund from cash flow.

wiki-russia.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Russia, a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to orient itself on the country at any given moment.
wiki-russia.recent: The 17 August peak sat on a cluster of stories out of Russia itself: a strike on Koloskovo in Belgorod that killed six including a 14-year-old, wildfires near Chelyabinsk burning over ground contaminated by the 1957 tank blast, and Kallas pressing the EU toward its broadest sanctions package. Putin's visit to the disputed Kurils drew a protest from Japan the day after.

wiki-pakistan.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of when a country of some 250 million, a nuclear arsenal and a contested border pulls the world's attention.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The late-July peak has drained away as the story moved to Islamabad's diplomacy: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed a joint defence pact whose text is not public, army chief Asim Munir carried Pakistan's Iran mediation to Tehran rather than the foreign ministry, and Moody's lifted the sovereign rating two notches to B3.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up on any given day, and which of its stories are pulling in readers beyond the ones already following it.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak followed America's accusation that China was evading tariffs, and came the day before Apple Intelligence's custom model was reported launching in China. Readers arrived again on 18-19 August, when LandSpace recovered a stainless-steel orbital booster after an orbital launch, the first such recovery by any country.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that every tanker leaving the Gulf must pass through, about two miles wide in each direction at its narrowest. Roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil crosses it, so its traffic count is a price signal for crude and gas alike.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the strait emptying. The 18 August peak followed an unknown projectile hitting a ship's engine room off Muscat, killing one crew member, a day after zero vessels transited on Sunday; Iran's Rezaei then warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, parliament approved fees on ships, and Monday saw a single gas carrier cross.

wiki-india.standing: The Wikipedia article on India, and how many people read it each day. Attention to a country's encyclopedia entry rises when something sends people looking for context, so the series works as a rough gauge of who is being drawn into a story from outside it.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on India's 80th Independence Day, when Modi used the address to renew his 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' push on semiconductor plants and energy security and to claim 650 new universities and doubled medical seats since 2014. Readership has drifted down since, to 25,210 on 23 August.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Readership rises when the country is at the centre of a story, so the count works as a rough gauge of how widely a Middle East event has travelled beyond the region.

wiki-ukraine.standing: The daily count of readers opening Wikipedia's article on Ukraine. It is a measure of public attention rather than events, and it rises when something happens that sends people looking for background on the country and its war.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The rise tracked a week that ended with allies convening in Kyiv on Independence Day, where Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023 and Britain agreed to let MBDA share SCALP missile component data with France and Ukraine. Before that came Russian missiles that killed at least 13 in Kyiv, and NABU searches of Zelenskyy's own office.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers. The count rises when a story about the country reaches an audience far beyond it.
wiki-nigeria.recent: The peak on Jul 27 has faded as the Osun election passed: civil society groups tallied 34 incidents and 18 deaths before Saturday's vote, rising to 56 incidents and 14 deaths in the count lawmakers later demanded a probe of, and Adeleke won re-election. Since then, attention has drifted down.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has emptied without a formal closure: one commodity vessel transited on Monday, down from six on Tuesday and nine the week before, after a projectile struck a ship's engine room off Muscat and killed a crew member. Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, and underwriters made the transit uninsurable.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits about an eighth below its 90-day baseline as Houthi attacks widened beyond the strait: six sailors died in a strike on a cargo ship on 11 August, and on 24 August a missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, far up the Red Sea. Maersk, rerouting around the closure, lifted profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic is running near its own 90-day baseline, down 3.4 percent over the last week, with no weather alert and waves at half a metre. The disruption in the coverage sits elsewhere on the same tanker routes — Hormuz traffic falling to single digits, a Houthi missile hitting a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu — rather than in the strait itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running about 11% above its 90-day baseline at 251 vessels a day, with no weather disruption. Nothing in the week's news points to a cause on the water: the friction around the strait has been legal and commercial rather than maritime, from Taiwan's indictment of nine people including an Nvidia manager over forged AI-server export paperwork to Beijing's recall of 3 million Teslas.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Daily transits sit near 33 vessels, about 4% below the canal's own 90-day baseline, having swung from 83 on 13 July to 22 on 22 July. Nothing in the record explains the drop; the separate dispute in which Hong Kong's CK Hutchison seeks HK$11.7b from Panama over canal ports concerns terminals, not transits.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen by roughly two thirds since June, tracking the attacks on Black Sea shipping: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea. Turkey says it is not in contact with Russia on a moratorium on military operations in the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has held close to its own 90-day baseline through the window, running near 150 vessels a day after a low of 111 on Jun 3 and a peak of 163 on Jun 13, with seas calm at 1.3 metres. Nothing in the sanctions campaign against Iran, or Rezaei's threat that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, has yet shifted the westbound flow here.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has been unremarkable: the count sits near 158 vessels a day, about 3.2 percent below its own 90-day baseline, with a high of 186 on Aug 1 and a low of 126 two days later. Seas have been calm, with waves peaking at 1.2 metres and no weather alert. Nothing in the window explains the swing.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic climbed as attacks pushed shipping off the Red Sea and Gulf routes: Houthi missiles hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, and Hormuz traffic fell to single digits as a 60-day US-Iran deadline expired. Rough weather is running alongside the surge, with waves to 2.7m.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, roughly 95 percent below its own 90-day baseline, as the Black Sea shipping war widened: a third Greek vessel in three days burned there, and Ukraine struck the Russian port of Novorossiysk in an overnight drone attack on 12 August. Owners are keeping hulls out of the basin.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its five-week range after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi-owned tanker off the kingdom's Red Sea coast, reopening a front Riyadh had believed it bought out of, and after Saudi artillery shelled villages in Yemen's Razih district on Monday. The Mecca defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey has not been published.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has recovered most of the ground lost since its 30 July low of 13,290, trading near 14,500 through a month in which Ankara's foreign commitments dominated the news: a joint defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and 70 long-range US missiles routed to Ukraine via Turkey over Moscow's objections.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Re-export and payments business through Dubai closed with it.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after climbing from 1,657 on 1 July to a high of 1,748 on 5 August, with little movement since. Nothing in the available material explains the rise.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed through August and set its high on Aug 21, after Prabowo named a central bank deputy as his nominee for governor on Aug 11 — a continuity pick the rupiah rose slightly on. Neither the Aug 16 Flores quake, which killed 53, nor the Bali ferry fire interrupted the run.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted lower over the quarter, from 26,040 on Jun 2 to 25,450, with a low of 22,670 on Jun 26 in between. Listings have kept coming — Shein is raising $1.77 billion in Hong Kong even as the US reviews it, and Alibaba sold new shares to raise $10 billion for AI rather than spend cash. The move itself is not explained by any single event here.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index has drifted down about 7% over the window, from its 22 June high of 4,163 to 3,876, with the floor at 3,764 on 17 July. No single market event in the record explains the slide; the period's news ran to industrial policy and trade friction — Evergrande's sentence, US accusations that China was evading tariffs, and a record 540,000 EVs exported in a month.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen through a summer of security shocks: North Korea fired a suspected ballistic missile on 12 August ahead of joint US-South Korea drills, and Washington then scrapped next month's Twin Dragons amphibious exercise, a pullback tied to force availability rather than diplomacy. Seoul's $880 billion AI bet has not offset it.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its June low, with the August 6 peak followed by a drift lower. Tata Group stocks fell in mid-August, with TCS down nearly 4 percent, while Modi renewed the push for semiconductor plants and energy security under 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' and Piyush Goyal took 200 firms to Japan to court semiconductor inputs.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth from its 10 June low to a 17 August high of 5768, with financial and payments activity in Singapore expanding through the run: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion as stablecoins moved into everyday use. A 70-member Indian delegation arrived on 19 August for trade and investment talks.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 22 high of 47,740 after bottoming at 39,930 on Jul 30, and the pressure around it is political as much as commercial. Taiwan indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager over AI server smuggling, while China's coast guard began patrolling east of Taiwan and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 39-day range after climbing from a 1,541 low on Jun 23 to a 1,639 high on Jul 17, though it gave up 2.4% on the day. Bangkok's diplomatic turn is the visible backdrop: Thailand's foreign minister met Lavrov in Moscow with trade up 23% in January-May 2026, and a deputy PM confirmed the government wants cybersecurity cooperation with Russia.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its late-May low, then dropped on the day. The impeachment trial of Sara Duterte has run through Manila all month: witnesses described confidential funds disbursed to names like Miggy Mango and Jay Kamote, and an ex-disbursing officer said Duterte ordered a P125-million transfer to a security officer.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index has climbed about 5 percent over the window to 9,151, peaking at 9,272 on Aug 6 before easing. The RBA held rates steady on 11 August as the housing market softened, and the professional-services slowdown reached the listed economy's edges: KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff on 24 August.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to 117,700 on Aug 21 from a Jul 23 low of 108,300, a gain of roughly 6% over the window, before easing 0.88% to 116,700. Nothing in the available reporting explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the window, from its 3 August high to a 18 August low, with the oil complex the one clear domestic story: Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast on 17 August, and Lula called the equatorial margin a "passport." Nothing in the window explains the wider drift.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits near the low end of its range after Washington cancelled the US visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, son of the former president, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. It touched 63,930 on Aug 18 before a 2.1% daily rebound.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits near the low of its 62-day range, down to 2,995,000 after a slide from the 22 July high of 3,380,000 and a 19 August trough. The one political event in the window is the 18 August arrest of a Milei adviser over the shooting of lawyer Nadia Beller in Santa Cruz de la Sierra; nothing in the record links it to the market's move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index sits near its high for the period despite the collapse of Canada-US trade talks: Washington imposed new tariffs on 22 August and Ottawa refused the relief offered on heavy trucks, vowing to match them dollar for dollar. Ontario Premier Doug Ford escalated further in Hamilton, threatening to cut electricity and mineral exports.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Washington spent the week widening its Iran campaign: Treasury Secretary Bessent named a revenue-wide sanctions programme "Economic Outcast" reaching third countries, and Iran's Rezaei answered that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz. Homeland Security separately proposed a $103,265 H-1B fee, a direct cost on the technology employers that dominate the index.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has drifted up over the window, reaching 10,910 on Jul 29 before easing to 10,850, a gain of about 3.5% from the Jun 9 low of 10,230. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index has climbed through the summer to 26,140, peaking at 26,440 on Aug 14 before easing. Frankfurt's own news flow ran to security rather than earnings: Kallas set out the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package on Aug 17, Croatia arrested a second Nord Stream suspect, and Berlin doubled its anti-drone force after an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index has drifted back from its 10 August high of 8,726 to 8,453, giving up a slim 0.37% on the day while holding a 2.4% gain over the window. The move has no single driver in the record: the French news of the period was regulatory and industrial rather than market-moving — the Conseil constitutionnel striking down the under-15 social media ban, jellyfish swarms knocking 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear generation offline at Gravelines.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed steadily to a high on Aug 13, with no single Dutch event in view driving it. Nearby news has been operational rather than financial: a cyberattack froze eight CEVA warehouses across Europe, and low water on the Rhine has cut barge draughts at Nijmegen.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index climbed to 20,210 on Aug 11 and has gained about 9% over the window, with utilities in focus as Spain extended the life of its largest nuclear plant in a policy U-turn on Aug 14. The coverage in this window otherwise concerns the Aug 12 total solar eclipse and does not explain the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range, a fifth of the way through a climb from 49,580 in late May to a 53,720 peak on 7 August, and has since drifted back to 52,540. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7% over the past 65 days, from a low of 13,220 on Jun 3 to a high of 14,630 on Aug 10, and has drifted sideways since. Nothing in the available record explains the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up 5.7% over the window and 1% on the day, after a high of 3327 on Aug 5. The available material does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index has given up roughly 9% across the past 64 days. It peaked at 4463 on May 25, fell to a low of 3966 on Jun 29, and has traded close to that floor since, ending at 4059 after a slight rise on the day. The available material does not explain the decline.

wiki-turkey.standing: The daily count of readers opening the English Wikipedia article on Turkey. It rises when the country enters a story large enough to send people looking for the basics — a war on its border, an alliance, an election.
wiki-turkey.recent: Readership climbed through August as Turkey took a central role in three separate stories: a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed in Mecca, whose text remains undisclosed and which names no obligations; the transfer of 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine via Turkey, which Moscow said undermines trust; and Israeli strikes on the Idlib airbase after Syria accepted Turkish troops.

xag.standing: Kinesis KAG is a token backed one-for-one by allocated physical silver, so its price tracks the metal. Silver is both a monetary hedge and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — which makes it swing harder than gold.
xag.recent: A low of 29.8 on Aug 6 and a high of 67.31 on Aug 20 bracket a month that ends at 62.33 — the price more than doubled within three weeks, even though the net change across the window is under 4%.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every fresh signal about where the central bank is heading.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract has climbed over the month, from 39 on Aug 1 to a high of 75 on Aug 15 and 65 now. Fed minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and traders had already been looking past CPI to the Fed's next tests. The market itself has had a turbulent month, with South Korea joining more than 30 jurisdictions restricting Polymarket access.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US refrains from striking Iran through a set date. It is a bet, not a forecast: the price is what traders will pay for the no-strike outcome, and it moves with every shift in Washington's posture.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The odds firmed as Washington swapped strikes for slow strangulation, with Treasury Secretary Bessent naming a revenue-wide sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast" and the US sanctioning Iranian nationals over a UK power plant intrusion. Tehran answered on paper rather than at sea — Rezaei's Hormuz shutdown threat, parliament's transit fees — while Munir carried a Trump message to Tehran.

wiki-lebanon.standing: Wikipedia readership for the country article, counted daily. It rises when Lebanon enters a news cycle, so the curve is a rough gauge of how many people outside the country are trying to catch up on it.
wiki-lebanon.recent: Readership tracked the strikes and their aftermath. An Israeli strike on a house near Ansar killed seven on 15 August, the same week strikes elsewhere in Lebanon killed 11 as talks between the US and Iran lapsed; the 21 August peak came as families in Beirut prepared their demand for an ICC trial over the 28 journalists killed since 2023.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The refined and crude liquid hydrocarbons that fuel most transport, and the feedstock behind plastics, fertiliser and asphalt. Its price sets freight and food costs, and its geography decides which states earn from the ground and which pay at the pump.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Attention tracked a fortnight of supply shocks rather than any single field. Shipping traffic in Hormuz slowed to a near halt on 17 August, a drone attack set Libya's Zawiya refinery alight, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved" in Russia. Pakistan raised diesel Rs6.47 to Rs390.42 a litre.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether US forces will invade Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it moves when the odds of a ground war shift rather than when the rhetoric does.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Washington swapped strikes for slow strangulation: officials moved to attrition, and Treasury Secretary Bessent named a revenue-wide sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast" that binds third countries through their banks. Trump called Munir before his Tehran trip, opening a Pakistani mediation channel, and Cairo has pressed Tehran for de-escalation.

wiki-syria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Syria — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are trying to understand the country at any moment, and one that tends to jump when the outside world's assumptions about it break.
wiki-syria.recent: The 11 August peak followed the death sentence handed to Bashar al-Assad in absentia, with 75 plaintiffs testifying against Atef Najib in a Damascus courtroom. Attention held through 18 August, when Syria granted the IAEA access to an Assad-era nuclear site concealed for 18 years and eight Israeli strikes hit one Idlib airbase, and again on 24 August, when Washington ended 47 years of Syria's terror listing.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a parliamentary majority for two decades, wins the most seats at the next State Duma election. It prices how firmly the Kremlin's governing party holds its legislative base.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The contract climbed from 56 on Jul 26 to a 74 high on Aug 16, the day Russia said it downed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight and Ukraine's deep-strike campaign reached one of its largest attacks of the war. Gasoline rationing followed in Moscow, with stations capping sales at 30 litres, and traders still paid more for continuity, not less.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran sign a final nuclear agreement by the end of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with diplomacy, sanctions and escalation rather than with any official process.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: The bet collapsed as Washington escalated instead of negotiating: Treasury Secretary Bessent named a revenue-wide sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast", the US sanctioned Iranian nationals over a UK power plant intrusion, and Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz. The 8% low on Aug 21 came as the rial hit a record 2.02 million per dollar.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 47th US president, whose readership rises and falls with the news cycle around him. Pageviews on it work as a rough daily gauge of how much of the world's attention American politics is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 11 August peak of 47,870 tracked the report that Trump left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck, switching planes after an Iranian threat; US spies later put low confidence in the plot claim. Attention slid to 30,490 by 15 August, then steadied as the Supreme Court denied his Carroll appeal without comment.

stocks:SPGI.standing: A financial information company whose ratings, indices and benchmarks sit inside the machinery of global markets — it grades sovereign and corporate debt, and its index business underpins funds holding trillions of dollars.
stocks:SPGI.recent: S&P found that 9,000 of 10,650 late-June excess deaths in Europe were people 65 and older, work that pushes heat mortality into underwriting. Its ratings arm remains the reference point rivals are measured against, with Moody's raising Pakistan two notches to B3 in the same window. The shares sit near the top of their range after a low of 405.2 on Aug 6.
